resolved_discrepancies.description: "The local finite-branch functions have Lipschitz gradients but lose second differentiability at the accumulation point" (13_L.tex:3) reads as a statement about all branches of the local construction. All four branches have globally Lipschitz gradients, but only three lose second differentiability: the branches f₀, f₁, f₂ of L:eq:embedding (and their whitened versions f_i(Az)) are not twice differentiable at zero, where the bad starts accumulate, while the fourth branch f₃(x)=μ‖x‖²/2+x₂ is a quadratic, twice differentiable everywhere, also after the whitening (Lean: branch_regularity). The chapter itself says it correctly at line 413 ("The first three branches ... fail to be twice differentiable at the accumulation point"). (Read as a statement about the objective F, "have Lipschitz gradients" would be false instead: F is not differentiable at 0.) Same wording issue as M8 (A/master/prose/009, A/verification/prose/017, A/lower_curvature/prose/010). Fix location: introductions['L'] in editorial/generate_companion.py (line 43), a hand-written chapter introduction, not a frozen source span.
resolved_discrepancies.proposed: Positive lower curvature requires a separate construction. The branches of the local finite-branch functions have Lipschitz gradients, and three of the four lose second differentiability at the accumulation point; no claim combines uniform strong convexity with the preceding local C2,1 branch regularity.

resolved_discrepancies.description: The last clause of Theorem L:thm:local (13_L.tex:59), "the latter version has a countable polyhedral nonsmooth part, not a finite smooth-branch representation", is false when read literally ("the latter version has no finite smooth-branch representation"), even for branches of the class of the theorem's own first version. The step scalar function is φ_b = max(-x, h₀, h₁) with h₀, h₁ convex and globally C^{1,1}: h_j = 0 for x ≤ 0; h_j = φ_b on the affine pieces between consecutive kinks κ_{n+1} < κ_n (κ_n = a_n(1+r)(b-1), with r = 1/128, a_n = r^n as at 13_L.tex:257) with n ≡ j (mod 2); on each other piece, the convex quadratic spline with one knot that matches the values of φ_b at both ends and the slopes of the two neighbouring pieces (possible because the slope of φ_b on the skipped piece lies strictly between them); beyond κ₀ the function that does not touch there continues affinely. The pieces are scaled copies of one profile, so h_j'' is bounded uniformly (about 171 for b = 1791/1024); the dips below φ_b have height O(a_n²) and slope O(a_n), so h_j is C^{1,1} also at 0. Hence F₂ = F_step(A·) is the maximum of ten globally C^{1,1}, uniformly strongly convex (modulus μλ_min(H̄₀)), globally gradient-Lipschitz branches: μ‖Az‖²/2 + k(q_iᵀAz) with k ∈ {-x, h₀, h₁} (h_j built for b = b_i), i = 0, 1, 2, and μ‖Az‖²/2 + (Az)₂ (a fortiori for C¹ branches). This is a sketch, checked with exact rational arithmetic at 2613 sample points of the pieces n = -1, …, 11 for b = b₀ = b₁ = 1791/1024 (independent review of 14 October 2026, scratch script c11_check.py; self-similarity extends it to all n, and the same construction works for b₂); it is not formalized in Lean. The descriptive reading (the nonsmooth part of the latter version is a countable polyhedral function, in contrast with the four smooth branches of the first version) is true and is what local_failure states (F₂(x) - xᵀBx/2 is the attained maximum of countably many affine functions); line 403 ("No claim of four smooth branches is made for this alternative") shows that it is the intended one. All other parts of the theorem are stated and proved by local_failure. Fix location: a logged transformation in editorial/generate_companion.py, since the clause is in the frozen span L.span.2 (corrected source bfgs_lean_stage1/master_report/latex/chapters/L.tex, lines 17-63; the clause is at line 52): a new if module=='L': replacement with its own logged kind and reason, like the module-D, I and C blocks (lines 115-131) or the module-E block (line 167). Not an entry of constant_range['L']: the reason logged for those entries (line 166) is shared and concerns the admissible line-search range.
resolved_discrepancies.proposed: Alternatively, it can be chosen so that its Hessian is one fixed positive-definite matrix wherever it is twice differentiable; the latter version has a countable polyhedral nonsmooth part. (Or: "…; the latter version is constructed from a countable polyhedral nonsmooth part rather than from four smooth branches.")
